chunks: And it was also narrated - from Dawud, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man died during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and he had no heir, so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave his inheritance to Hamshahirij.

This is a marsi (disconnected) narration and does not contradict what we have previously presented from the reports, even though there is nothing in it that opposes what preceded, because what it contained was that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave his estate to Hamsharij, and perhaps he did that as a form of administrative discretion (istihsan), because if the wealth was exclusively his, as we have mentioned, it was permissible for him to do with it as he wished, and the narration does not state that this is the ruling for all wealth that has no heir, which would be contrary to the previously mentioned reports.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali handle the inheritance of someone with no heirs?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites this report to demonstrate that Imam Ali’s (AS) distribution of the estate to Hamshahirij was likely an act of administrative discretion (istihsan) rather than a binding universal legal ruling, thereby avoiding contradiction with other hadiths. This highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the Imam’s actions in specific instances may reflect practical governance or personal choice rather than establishing a fixed jurisprudential precedent for all cases of *māl al-gharīr*.
